current.critique: The round 24 wing as it stands still has the tension it was pitched with. Every patch adds weight, and nothing in it says why a wing that is half repairs should carry Lumi further than one good build, so the scars risk being decoration and the beach a chore. The bend-under-air-load coupling that 'heavier here, stiffer there' needs is buried in one road step, ready to be faked with a mass offset, and the bird only jumps on step four. The strength is real: a spar breaking where the beam stress really beat the cane is the honest failure the human asks for, and 'no two wings alike' is a hook people would describe the game by.

goals.title: The wing that remembers every crash
goals.critique: This is round 24's wing again, but it answers the two faults named there and so earns more than a reword. Wash-in from a soft tip, fed back through a vortex lattice of the bent shape, is a true, visible reason a splinted wing beats a fresh one, and the slow-motion replay of the tip curling before the dive is a clip people would send, a better moment than 'three metres short'. Lumi now jumps on the first step and the coupling is checked against a cantilever and a divergence speed, which makes it hard to fake. The weak side is that the player hardly decides anything: the crash names the spot and the splint goes there, so the loop risks turning into following instructions. It also converges, because once the weak places are stiff the wing just works and the far island ends it, with the materials map from round 24 shrunk to one line of bamboo at the end. 'Flies further than any fresh one' is only true while fresh wings stay crude, and the Learn to Fly shadow keeps memorable from climbing.
